sections.changelog:
0.3.5

  • Open the responsive accessibility panel below the sticky header without covering the menu, brand, or docked toggle.
  • Keep the full accessibility panel inside short landscape viewports with an independent scroll area.

0.3.4

  • Keep the responsive header dock attached while scrolling even when the active theme sets its own document overflow rules.
  • Preserve the mobile drawer scroll lock with an explicit open-state override.

0.3.3

  • Dock the responsive accessibility control inside a reserved sticky header area so it cannot cover prose, calls to action, or footer controls.
  • Verify closed, open, restored, top-of-page, scrolled, and short-landscape accessibility states at exact responsive boundaries.

0.3.2

  • Keep the mobile menu control visible through hover and keyboard focus at responsive widths.
  • Keep desktop search states on the intended high-contrast palette and move the responsive accessibility control into a compact bottom-left rail.
  • Test touch rendering separately from pointer, keyboard, hover, and focus interaction states, with clean screenshot segments and exact overlap.

0.3.1

  • Restore visible, high-contrast labels across managed real-estate actions.
  • Hide the menu control above its exact breakpoint and restore opening focus after close.
  • Strengthen the drawer presentation and move the accessibility toolbar away from the page header.
  • Capture very long production pages in reliable visual segments.

0.3.0

  • Add a national Thailand real-estate hub connected to seven existing guides.
  • Add exact ID and path bindings, keyword-led metadata, self-canonicals, visible breadcrumbs, and contextual continuations.
  • Add a shared RTL header, mobile drawer, search, footer, responsive artwork, source panels, and article navigation.
  • Connect the homepage menu, search, shortcuts, sections, and footer to the released real-estate and business owners.
  • Add deterministic content and SEO migration contracts plus anonymous live acceptance checks.

0.2.7

  • Use the current homepage description and artwork for Open Graph and X shares.
  • Hide and inert both external accessibility controls while the mobile navigation drawer is open, then restore their prior state exactly.
  • Close the mobile drawer and move focus to the visible header when the desktop breakpoint is crossed.
  • Add anonymous production acceptance checks for social metadata, structured data, language, interactions, responsive layout, and drawer focus behavior.

0.2.6

  • Add the canonical Thailand country, seven-region, and 77-province registry.
  • Add exact Hebrew, English, and Thai identity resolution without fuzzy guesses.
  • Add the cacheable public geography endpoint with ETag revalidation.
  • Add SEO intent ownership and release evidence for geography source lineage.
  • Add concrete Chabad and kosher-service details for Bangkok, Phuket, Samui, Koh Phangan, and Chiang Mai.
  • Replace unsupported search labels and vague homepage copy, and enforce a 50-phrase public language boundary.

0.2.5

  • Replace presentation-style homepage language with direct destination, property, business, living, and reader language.
  • Keep unsolicited chat greetings compact without closing a visitor-initiated chat.

0.2.4

  • Resume chat settling when a visitor returns through browser history.

0.2.3

  • Wait for the chat widget to confirm its compact state after a late load.

0.2.2

  • Reserve the correct side of the phone action bar for the existing chat launcher.

0.2.1

  • Keep the existing chat widget compact on larger screens and clear of homepage controls on phones.
  • Add release checks for the responsive chat behavior.

0.2.0

  • Add the RTL homepage experience behind an administrator-controlled, fail-closed feature flag.
  • Add scoped dependency-free assets, responsive WebP artwork, private canary controls, SEO coexistence safeguards, and cache-safe rollback.

0.1.0

  • Add the bounded, no-write platform bootstrap and public release healthcheck.
